work.title: Plato, Apology
work.notes: Socrates wrote no philosophical works. The Apology is Plato's literary representation of his defence; preserve Plato's authorship and distinguish dramatic speech from a verbatim trial transcript.

edition.label: Henry Cary English translation with Edward Brooks introduction; Project Gutenberg #13726
edition.licenseNote: Project Gutenberg metadata states public domain in the USA; verify the law of the deployment jurisdiction before production redistribution. Separate Plato's dialogue from Brooks's modern introduction.

passages.translationText: When I left him, I reasoned thus with myself: I am wiser than this man, for neither of us appears to know anything great and good; but he fancies he knows something, although he knows nothing; whereas I, as I do not know anything, so I do not fancy I do. In this trifling particular, then, I appear to be wiser than he, because I do not fancy I know what I do not know.
passages.interpretiveNote: Cary's version provides an independent historical translation of the wisdom passage: Socrates' advantage lies in refusing to pretend to knowledge he lacks.
passages.period: Platonic representation of Socrates; historical English translation
